paragraphs: Hitchin is in North Hertfordshire, so children in care from the town are looked after by Hertfordshire County Council's own fostering service and by the agencies shown above. The council runs its service on a not-for-profit basis, and its training is held at its offices in Stevenage and Apsley.

In the autumn of 2025 the council brought its HELP campaign to Hitchin, inviting local people to find out about fostering and to help spread the word by sharing posts, hosting talks in community groups or handing out leaflets. At the time the council's lead member for children's social care said Hertfordshire had around 1,000 children in its care and fewer than 400 foster families, which is why the campaign asks so plainly for more carers.

To foster with the council you need at least one spare bedroom and to be over 21 and in reasonable health. Carers receive a weekly payment as well as an allowance for each child. The council describes monthly supervision from a dedicated social worker, a buddy who already fosters, support groups and coffee mornings, help with education, special needs and mental health, a duty social worker when your own is away, and an out-of-hours line seven days a week. It is also part of Foster East, a partnership of eleven councils across the East of England.

The council holds information evenings most months, mainly online; the next is on Thursday 10 December 2026, from 7pm. Our Hertfordshire page covers the whole county, and our Stevenage and Luton pages cover the towns nearby. Speak to the council and to two or three of the services above, and ask each about the children they most need homes for, training and support.
